I read the spec and cross-checked every load-bearing claim against the code, the fixtures, the vendored `async-openai` 0.41.3 source, and every in-repo `ModelEvent` consumer.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES

The chosen implementation (EOF-anchored `finish()`) is correct and should survive verbatim — I verified the `[DONE]` behaviour, the single finish site, the fixture-invisibility argument, and the Responses-immunity claim, and all four hold. But four load-bearing *justification* claims are refuted by code in this repository: the Bedrock comparison that decides the design, the stated impact on SMA-402, the "multi-choice preserved exactly" equivalence, and the out-of-scope Bedrock ticket. The test plan is also thinner than the spec's own "mutation check" rhetoric implies. The BLOCKER below is confined to rationale/follow-up sections, but it must be fixed *before* the PR body and Linear issues are written, because it publicly asserts a bug in a sibling crate that does not exist.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The Bedrock comparison table — the spec's sole stated reason for its design choice — is refuted by the Bedrock code** — The spec (lines 81–101) characterises Bedrock as "emit `[Usage, Finish]` on the usage event" and scores it "**no `Finish` at all** ❌" when the trailing event never arrives. Bedrock already has exactly the EOF flush the spec is proposing to add: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:262` (`pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self) -> Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>`, doc-commented *"Flush any buffered stop reason when the Bedrock stream ends normally (EOF) without having emitted a `Metadata` event"*), driven from `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:107-112` (`Ok(None) => { if let Some(terminal) = translator.finish() { yield terminal; } return; }`). Bedrock is therefore a *hybrid* — pair-on-Metadata **plus** EOF flush — and is not vulnerable to the failure the table attributes to it. Consequently out-of-scope item 1 ("Bedrock truncation gap", spec line 237) describes a bug that does not exist. | Why it matters: the design decision is presented as forced by evidence, and the evidence is wrong; a false Linear issue would be filed against a published crate, and the PR body would publicly claim a sibling provider is broken. It also means the implementer will not read the pattern they are supposedly copying. | Suggested fix: rewrite the "Rejected: Bedrock pattern" section to say Bedrock is *already* EOF-safe and that the real reason to prefer the Gemini shape is simplicity (one emission site, no `metadata_seen`/`pending_stop_reason` interaction, no dependence on a trailing chunk that Appendix A.2 shows may never arrive). Delete out-of-scope item 1's "truncation gap" and replace it with the genuine defect: the misread `Usage must precede Finish` comment at `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:14` and `:439`.

### MAJOR

- **The stated impact ("SMA-402 silently under-counts every OpenAI turn") is false for this repository** — Every in-repo consumer drains the model stream to `None` before reading usage: the agent loop at `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:941-999` (`while let Some(evt) = model_stream.next().await { acc.observe(&ev); … }` then `acc.finish()`), the Temporal activity at `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:98`, and `RetryingModel` at `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:222-232` (verbatim forward). So the trailing `Usage` *is* observed today and nothing under-counts. | Why it matters: the ticket's justification is falsifiable and will land in a CHANGELOG; a reviewer who checks it will conclude the fix is cosmetic. | Suggested fix: restate the impact honestly — this is a **contract-conformance** fix for external consumers, plus (see next finding) it removes duplicate `Finish` emission. And cite the real in-repo Finish-terminated consumer the spec missed: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:237` — `ModelEvent::Finish { .. } => break,`. It ignores `Usage` (`_ => {}`) so it is harmless *today*, but it proves the "stops reading at `Finish`" pattern is not hypothetical, and it is the honest evidence for the ticket.

- **"Multi-choice last-wins semantics are preserved" (spec line 79) is wrong — the change is not equivalent under `n > 1`** — `finish_event` today is a **per-`consume` local** (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:244`, pushed at `:298`), so the current code emits one `Finish` **per chunk that carries any `finish_reason`**. Moving it to a struct field collapses that to exactly one `Finish` at EOF. Counter-example: chunk A `choices:[{index:0,delta:{},finish_reason:"stop"}]`, chunk B `choices:[{index:1,delta:{content:"x"}}]`, chunk C `choices:[{index:1,delta:{},finish_reason:"length"}]` → old emits `Finish(Stop), TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`; new emits `TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`. The same divergence occurs on the far more likely single-choice case where a proxy repeats `finish_reason` on the usage chunk (Appendix A.1 shows LiteLLM does *not*, but that is one proxy). | Why it matters: the spec tells the implementer there is nothing to think about here, so no test will pin it; and "old code emits `Finish` then more deltas" is itself a contract violation the fix silently repairs — an unclaimed benefit. | Suggested fix: replace the "preserved exactly" sentence with the actual semantics ("exactly one `Finish` per stream; the last observed `finish_reason` across the whole stream wins"), note that this also eliminates duplicate `Finish` emission, and add the multi-choice/repeated-`finish_reason` case as a unit test on `ChatTranslator`.

- **`tests/chat_wire.rs` encodes the same non-occurring wire shape and states the falsehood in prose — and is not in scope** — `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs:34-41` builds an inline SSE body that welds `usage` onto the `finish_reason` chunk, above the comment *"Usage arrives on the same chunk as `finish_reason` (per OpenAI's `stream_options.include_usage: true` behaviour)"* — precisely the claim Appendix A refutes. The spec's Fixtures section (lines 154–166) names only the two `tests/fixtures/*.txt` files. | Why it matters: the spec argues "the fixtures are the entire regression signal" and "re-recording is the substance", then leaves the third instance — the one that documents the false belief in English — untouched. | Suggested fix: add `tests/chat_wire.rs` to the Fixtures section: restructure the inline body to the captured trailing-usage envelope and delete/correct the comment.

- **The identical misread doc comment survives 200 lines away in the same crate** — The spec (change 5, line 136) corrects `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:237-241`, but the byte-identical assertion lives at `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:274-278` (*"Event ordering follows the 'Usage before Finish' contract stated in `Model::invoke`"*), plus bedrock `stream.rs:14` and `:439`. | Why it matters: the spec identifies this misreading as the root cause ("that misreading is what made inline `Finish` look correct") and then leaves it in place in the same crate and the same PR, where it is a one-line edit. | Suggested fix: fix `responses.rs:274-278` in this PR; defer only the bedrock ones.

- **The `Some(Err(_))` arm silently discards a buffered `Finish` — a behaviour change vs. today that is neither stated nor tested** — Today, if the stream errors *after* the finish chunk, the consumer has already received `Finish` (emitted inline) and then gets `Err`. Under the new design, `chat.rs:78-81` returns without calling `finish()`, so the consumer gets `Err` and **no** `Finish` at all. This is not theoretical for the audience the spec invokes (SMA-451 proxies): `CreateChatCompletionStreamResponse` requires `id`, `choices`, `created`, `model`, `object` as non-`Option` fields (`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/async-openai-0.41.3/src/types/chat/chat_.rs:1178-1200`), so a proxy that omits `object` on its trailing usage chunk produces a deserialization `Err` mid-stream — and now the turn ends with no terminal event where before it had one. The Exit-path table (spec line 151) lists this row but does not disclose the delta. | Why it matters: the spec's own selling point is "never trade an ordering violation for a missing terminal event", and this exit path does exactly that. | Suggested fix: either state and defend the choice explicitly in the table ("buffered `Finish` is discarded on error — the turn did not complete cleanly"), or flush `finish()` before yielding `Err`. Add a test with a fixture whose last chunk is malformed JSON so the decision is pinned either way. Also worth noting: the Gemini driver logs-and-`continue`s on an unparseable chunk (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:159-169`) where OpenAI kills the stream — an asymmetry the "proxy compatibility" argument should acknowledge.

- **Only one of the four proposed tests can fail on the pre-fix code, and its assertions are weaker than they need to be** — I traced each: test 1 (trailing-usage fixture, `Finish` last + `Usage` before it) genuinely goes red pre-fix — confirmed, that one is real. Test 3 ("no-usage stream still emits exactly one `Finish`") and test 4 ("truncated stream emits no `Finish`") **both pass on the pre-fix translator** — pre-fix emits `Finish` inline on the finish chunk and emits none when `finish_reason` is absent. They are guards against the *new* code's failure modes (a forgotten `finish()` call), which is fine, but the spec's "mutation check" framing (lines 200–204) implies all of them discriminate. Missing entirely: cancel-after-finish-chunk, error-after-finish-chunk, and any test of `n > 1`. | Why it matters: the spec's central lesson is "a test that cannot fail on broken code is the failure mode that let this ship" — and three of its four tests are that. | Suggested fix: (a) label tests 3/4 as new-code guards, not regressions; (b) strengthen test 1 to assert *exactly one* `Finish` and the actual token counts (`input_tokens: 8, output_tokens: 6` from A.1), so a translator emitting a zeroed `Usage` cannot pass; (c) add a cancellation test that fires the token after the finish chunk and asserts no `Finish` (the existing `tests/cancellation.rs:22` cancels before the first chunk and does not cover the new race); (d) add cheap `ChatTranslator` unit tests (`consume` + `finish`) next to the existing ones at `chat.rs:378-541` — that is the natural place to pin multi-choice and no-`finish_reason` semantics without wiremock.

- **The follow-up "truncation gap" ticket points at the wrong crate — Anthropic has it, Bedrock does not** — `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:161-169` buffers `stop_reason` from `message_delta` and only emits `Finish` on `message_stop`, and its driver at `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:113` is a bare `None => return` with no EOF flush. A stream truncated between `message_delta` and `message_stop` therefore emits `Usage` and no `Finish`, where Gemini, Bedrock, and post-fix OpenAI would all emit one. | Why it matters: the cross-provider follow-up is scoped from a wrong inventory, so the one provider that actually has the gap is not on the list. | Suggested fix: retarget out-of-scope item 1 at `providers-anthropic`, and have the conformance follow-up (item 2) explicitly assert "EOF after an observed stop reason emits `Finish`" across all five providers, not just "streams end with `Finish`".

### MINOR

- **"Transcribed verbatim" contradicts the elision in Appendix A.1** — Line 261 says "Middle content deltas elided; the tail is verbatim", but line 156 says the fixture is "transcribed verbatim from the capture". The middle of the fixture must be reconstructed by hand. Given the section's whole point is provenance honesty, say which lines are captured and which are reconstructed.
- **The capture is LiteLLM's mock, not `api.openai.com`** — The A.1 usage chunk carries `"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}]`; OpenAI's own API sends `"choices":[]` on the usage chunk (as async-openai's own field doc at `chat_.rs:1181` states: *"Can also be empty for the last chunk if you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`"*). Both parse identically through `consume` (I checked — the choices loop simply doesn't run), so this is low-risk, but the fixture will be named as the OpenAI provenance anchor while encoding a proxy-specific envelope. State the limitation, and consider a second hand-authored variant with `"choices":[]`.
- **The provenance-comment syntax is unspecified** — Spec line 165 says "Each fixture gets a leading comment". These files are fed to a real SSE parser via wiremock, so the comment must be a `:`-prefixed SSE comment line. A `#` or `//` line would be parsed as an unknown field name (harmless but silently wrong) and sets a bad precedent for the anthropic fixtures, which are split on literal `\n` by their tests.
- **No observability on the "stream ended with no `finish_reason`" path** — `finish()` returning empty is the one silent exit that produces a turn with no terminal event. A `tracing::debug!(target: "paigasus::openai::chat", …)` there costs nothing and makes truncation distinguishable from a clean stop in a trace. (Gemini doesn't log either — that's a reason to start, not to skip.)
- **`finish()`'s return shape is a third variant** — Gemini returns `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (`providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:73`), Bedrock returns `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (`providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:262`), and the spec proposes `Vec<ModelEvent>`. Fine locally, but the conformance follow-up should pick one; say which.
- **Adjacent stale comments** — `chat.rs:120` and `chat.rs:179` say "async-openai 0.40"; `Cargo.lock` pins 0.41.3. Since change 5 already edits comments in this file, sweeping these is free.
- **A cancellation race changes shape** — If the token fires between the finish chunk and EOF, the new code emits no `Finish` where the old code already had. This is contract-correct (`core/src/model.rs:65-67`) and benign in-repo (`ModelTurnAccumulator` defaults `finish_reason` to `Stop`), but it belongs in the Exit-path table as a delta rather than as an unremarked row.

### QUESTIONS

- Was the trailing-usage ordering confirmed against `api.openai.com`, or only against LiteLLM? The ticket generalises to "OpenAI"; the evidence is one proxy's mock backend. If it can't be confirmed, say so in the spec rather than letting the fixture name imply it.
- `ModelSettings` has no `n` field and `build_request` never sets one, so `n > 1` can only arrive from a nonstandard proxy. Should the translator *warn* when it sees a second distinct `finish_reason` (i.e. genuinely ambiguous multi-choice), rather than silently last-wins?
- Should the OpenAI driver tolerate an unparseable chunk the way Gemini does (log + `continue`) instead of terminating the stream? This directly affects the SMA-451 proxy audience the design section invokes as its motivation.
- The Responses immunity argument as written ("they cannot be split across chunks") is true but fragile. The durable invariant is "`Usage` is constructed *only* inside `terminal_events`, which unconditionally appends `Finish`". Should that be recorded as a comment/test so a future arm that emits partial usage doesn't silently break it?
- `ResponseFailed`/`ResponseError` yield `Err` with no `Finish` (`responses.rs:408-426`) — I checked this against the core contract and it is consistent (core mandates that `Finish` is terminal, never that it is mandatory). The spec's "verified immune" note should state this explicitly, since "is there a path with no terminal event at all?" is the exact question the issue asked to discharge.

## What's good

- **Every line reference in the spec is accurate** — I spot-checked eight (`core/src/model.rs:55-63` and `:65-67`, `chat.rs:242-303` and `:237-241`, `responses.rs:441-483`, `gemini/src/model.rs:150,156`, `bedrock/src/stream.rs:14-22`, `chat_streaming.rs:25-33`) and all resolve to what the spec says they do. That is rarer than it should be.
- **The three hardest technical claims are correct, and I verified each independently.** (1) `async-openai` 0.41.3 does consume `[DONE]` internally and ends iteration — `client.rs:811-813` (wasm `unfold` → `None`) and `client.rs:860-862` (non-wasm task `break` → channel close → `None`), so the `None` arm really is the single finish site. (2) The "behaviourally invisible against the current fixtures" argument is exactly right: tracing `consume` over `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt:13` gives `[Usage, Finish]` before and `[Usage]` + `[Finish]` after — an identical emitted sequence. That argument is the strongest thing in the document and it holds. (3) The Responses backend is genuinely immune: `Usage` is only ever built inside `terminal_events` (`responses.rs:455-462`), which unconditionally pushes `Finish` at `:481`, and no other arm emits `Usage`.
- **The release / README / mdBook calls are all correct.** `ChatTranslator` is `pub(crate)` (`chat.rs:216`) inside a private `mod backend` (`src/lib.rs:22`), the crate exports only `OpenAiModel`/`OpenAiModelBuilder`/`BuildError` (`lib.rs:29-30`), the openai README says nothing about usage or ordering, and `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:55-57` documents `Finish` as terminal without asserting any `Usage` position — so no book edit is owed. The no-manual-bump call also matches CLAUDE.md's already-released-crate rule. The `.gitattributes` analysis (CRLF still parses because wiremock hands bytes to a real SSE parser) is likewise correct, and adding the rule as defence-not-fix is the right call, honestly framed.

I read the spec and cross-checked every load-bearing claim against the code, the fixtures, the vendored `async-openai` 0.41.3 source, and every in-repo `ModelEvent` consumer.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES

The chosen implementation (EOF-anchored `finish()`) is correct and should survive verbatim — I verified the `[DONE]` behaviour, the single finish site, the fixture-invisibility argument, and the Responses-immunity claim, and all four hold. But four load-bearing *justification* claims are refuted by code in this repository: the Bedrock comparison that decides the design, the stated impact on SMA-402, the "multi-choice preserved exactly" equivalence, and the out-of-scope Bedrock ticket. The test plan is also thinner than the spec's own "mutation check" rhetoric implies. The BLOCKER below is confined to rationale/follow-up sections, but it must be fixed *before* the PR body and Linear issues are written, because it publicly asserts a bug in a sibling crate that does not exist.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The Bedrock comparison table — the spec's sole stated reason for its design choice — is refuted by the Bedrock code** — The spec (lines 81–101) characterises Bedrock as "emit `[Usage, Finish]` on the usage event" and scores it "**no `Finish` at all** ❌" when the trailing event never arrives. Bedrock already has exactly the EOF flush the spec is proposing to add: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:262` (`pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self) -> Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>`, doc-commented *"Flush any buffered stop reason when the Bedrock stream ends normally (EOF) without having emitted a `Metadata` event"*), driven from `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:107-112` (`Ok(None) => { if let Some(terminal) = translator.finish() { yield terminal; } return; }`). Bedrock is therefore a *hybrid* — pair-on-Metadata **plus** EOF flush — and is not vulnerable to the failure the table attributes to it. Consequently out-of-scope item 1 ("Bedrock truncation gap", spec line 237) describes a bug that does not exist. | Why it matters: the design decision is presented as forced by evidence, and the evidence is wrong; a false Linear issue would be filed against a published crate, and the PR body would publicly claim a sibling provider is broken. It also means the implementer will not read the pattern they are supposedly copying. | Suggested fix: rewrite the "Rejected: Bedrock pattern" section to say Bedrock is *already* EOF-safe and that the real reason to prefer the Gemini shape is simplicity (one emission site, no `metadata_seen`/`pending_stop_reason` interaction, no dependence on a trailing chunk that Appendix A.2 shows may never arrive). Delete out-of-scope item 1's "truncation gap" and replace it with the genuine defect: the misread `Usage must precede Finish` comment at `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:14` and `:439`.

### MAJOR

- **The stated impact ("SMA-402 silently under-counts every OpenAI turn") is false for this repository** — Every in-repo consumer drains the model stream to `None` before reading usage: the agent loop at `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:941-999` (`while let Some(evt) = model_stream.next().await { acc.observe(&ev); … }` then `acc.finish()`), the Temporal activity at `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:98`, and `RetryingModel` at `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:222-232` (verbatim forward). So the trailing `Usage` *is* observed today and nothing under-counts. | Why it matters: the ticket's justification is falsifiable and will land in a CHANGELOG; a reviewer who checks it will conclude the fix is cosmetic. | Suggested fix: restate the impact honestly — this is a **contract-conformance** fix for external consumers, plus (see next finding) it removes duplicate `Finish` emission. And cite the real in-repo Finish-terminated consumer the spec missed: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:237` — `ModelEvent::Finish { .. } => break,`. It ignores `Usage` (`_ => {}`) so it is harmless *today*, but it proves the "stops reading at `Finish`" pattern is not hypothetical, and it is the honest evidence for the ticket.

- **"Multi-choice last-wins semantics are preserved" (spec line 79) is wrong — the change is not equivalent under `n > 1`** — `finish_event` today is a **per-`consume` local** (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:244`, pushed at `:298`), so the current code emits one `Finish` **per chunk that carries any `finish_reason`**. Moving it to a struct field collapses that to exactly one `Finish` at EOF. Counter-example: chunk A `choices:[{index:0,delta:{},finish_reason:"stop"}]`, chunk B `choices:[{index:1,delta:{content:"x"}}]`, chunk C `choices:[{index:1,delta:{},finish_reason:"length"}]` → old emits `Finish(Stop), TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`; new emits `TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`. The same divergence occurs on the far more likely single-choice case where a proxy repeats `finish_reason` on the usage chunk (Appendix A.1 shows LiteLLM does *not*, but that is one proxy). | Why it matters: the spec tells the implementer there is nothing to think about here, so no test will pin it; and "old code emits `Finish` then more deltas" is itself a contract violation the fix silently repairs — an unclaimed benefit. | Suggested fix: replace the "preserved exactly" sentence with the actual semantics ("exactly one `Finish` per stream; the last observed `finish_reason` across the whole stream wins"), note that this also eliminates duplicate `Finish` emission, and add the multi-choice/repeated-`finish_reason` case as a unit test on `ChatTranslator`.

- **`tests/chat_wire.rs` encodes the same non-occurring wire shape and states the falsehood in prose — and is not in scope** — `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs:34-41` builds an inline SSE body that welds `usage` onto the `finish_reason` chunk, above the comment *"Usage arrives on the same chunk as `finish_reason` (per OpenAI's `stream_options.include_usage: true` behaviour)"* — precisely the claim Appendix A refutes. The spec's Fixtures section (lines 154–166) names only the two `tests/fixtures/*.txt` files. | Why it matters: the spec argues "the fixtures are the entire regression signal" and "re-recording is the substance", then leaves the third instance — the one that documents the false belief in English — untouched. | Suggested fix: add `tests/chat_wire.rs` to the Fixtures section: restructure the inline body to the captured trailing-usage envelope and delete/correct the comment.

- **The identical misread doc comment survives 200 lines away in the same crate** — The spec (change 5, line 136) corrects `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:237-241`, but the byte-identical assertion lives at `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:274-278` (*"Event ordering follows the 'Usage before Finish' contract stated in `Model::invoke`"*), plus bedrock `stream.rs:14` and `:439`. | Why it matters: the spec identifies this misreading as the root cause ("that misreading is what made inline `Finish` look correct") and then leaves it in place in the same crate and the same PR, where it is a one-line edit. | Suggested fix: fix `responses.rs:274-278` in this PR; defer only the bedrock ones.

- **The `Some(Err(_))` arm silently discards a buffered `Finish` — a behaviour change vs. today that is neither stated nor tested** — Today, if the stream errors *after* the finish chunk, the consumer has already received `Finish` (emitted inline) and then gets `Err`. Under the new design, `chat.rs:78-81` returns without calling `finish()`, so the consumer gets `Err` and **no** `Finish` at all. This is not theoretical for the audience the spec invokes (SMA-451 proxies): `CreateChatCompletionStreamResponse` requires `id`, `choices`, `created`, `model`, `object` as non-`Option` fields (`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/async-openai-0.41.3/src/types/chat/chat_.rs:1178-1200`), so a proxy that omits `object` on its trailing usage chunk produces a deserialization `Err` mid-stream — and now the turn ends with no terminal event where before it had one. The Exit-path table (spec line 151) lists this row but does not disclose the delta. | Why it matters: the spec's own selling point is "never trade an ordering violation for a missing terminal event", and this exit path does exactly that. | Suggested fix: either state and defend the choice explicitly in the table ("buffered `Finish` is discarded on error — the turn did not complete cleanly"), or flush `finish()` before yielding `Err`. Add a test with a fixture whose last chunk is malformed JSON so the decision is pinned either way. Also worth noting: the Gemini driver logs-and-`continue`s on an unparseable chunk (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/model.rs:159-169`) where OpenAI kills the stream — an asymmetry the "proxy compatibility" argument should acknowledge.

- **Only one of the four proposed tests can fail on the pre-fix code, and its assertions are weaker than they need to be** — I traced each: test 1 (trailing-usage fixture, `Finish` last + `Usage` before it) genuinely goes red pre-fix — confirmed, that one is real. Test 3 ("no-usage stream still emits exactly one `Finish`") and test 4 ("truncated stream emits no `Finish`") **both pass on the pre-fix translator** — pre-fix emits `Finish` inline on the finish chunk and emits none when `finish_reason` is absent. They are guards against the *new* code's failure modes (a forgotten `finish()` call), which is fine, but the spec's "mutation check" framing (lines 200–204) implies all of them discriminate. Missing entirely: cancel-after-finish-chunk, error-after-finish-chunk, and any test of `n > 1`. | Why it matters: the spec's central lesson is "a test that cannot fail on broken code is the failure mode that let this ship" — and three of its four tests are that. | Suggested fix: (a) label tests 3/4 as new-code guards, not regressions; (b) strengthen test 1 to assert *exactly one* `Finish` and the actual token counts (`input_tokens: 8, output_tokens: 6` from A.1), so a translator emitting a zeroed `Usage` cannot pass; (c) add a cancellation test that fires the token after the finish chunk and asserts no `Finish` (the existing `tests/cancellation.rs:22` cancels before the first chunk and does not cover the new race); (d) add cheap `ChatTranslator` unit tests (`consume` + `finish`) next to the existing ones at `chat.rs:378-541` — that is the natural place to pin multi-choice and no-`finish_reason` semantics without wiremock.

- **The follow-up "truncation gap" ticket points at the wrong crate — Anthropic has it, Bedrock does not** — `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-522-openai-finish-usage-order/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:161-169` buffers `stop_reason` from `message_delta` and only emits `Finish` on `message_stop`, and its driver at `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:113` is a bare `None => return` with no EOF flush. A stream truncated between `message_delta` and `message_stop` therefore emits `Usage` and no `Finish`, where Gemini, Bedrock, and post-fix OpenAI would all emit one. | Why it matters: the cross-provider follow-up is scoped from a wrong inventory, so the one provider that actually has the gap is not on the list. | Suggested fix: retarget out-of-scope item 1 at `providers-anthropic`, and have the conformance follow-up (item 2) explicitly assert "EOF after an observed stop reason emits `Finish`" across all five providers, not just "streams end with `Finish`".

### MINOR

- **"Transcribed verbatim" contradicts the elision in Appendix A.1** — Line 261 says "Middle content deltas elided; the tail is verbatim", but line 156 says the fixture is "transcribed verbatim from the capture". The middle of the fixture must be reconstructed by hand. Given the section's whole point is provenance honesty, say which lines are captured and which are reconstructed.
- **The capture is LiteLLM's mock, not `api.openai.com`** — The A.1 usage chunk carries `"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}]`; OpenAI's own API sends `"choices":[]` on the usage chunk (as async-openai's own field doc at `chat_.rs:1181` states: *"Can also be empty for the last chunk if you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`"*). Both parse identically through `consume` (I checked — the choices loop simply doesn't run), so this is low-risk, but the fixture will be named as the OpenAI provenance anchor while encoding a proxy-specific envelope. State the limitation, and consider a second hand-authored variant with `"choices":[]`.
- **The provenance-comment syntax is unspecified** — Spec line 165 says "Each fixture gets a leading comment". These files are fed to a real SSE parser via wiremock, so the comment must be a `:`-prefixed SSE comment line. A `#` or `//` line would be parsed as an unknown field name (harmless but silently wrong) and sets a bad precedent for the anthropic fixtures, which are split on literal `\n` by their tests.
- **No observability on the "stream ended with no `finish_reason`" path** — `finish()` returning empty is the one silent exit that produces a turn with no terminal event. A `tracing::debug!(target: "paigasus::openai::chat", …)` there costs nothing and makes truncation distinguishable from a clean stop in a trace. (Gemini doesn't log either — that's a reason to start, not to skip.)
- **`finish()`'s return shape is a third variant** — Gemini returns `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (`providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:73`), Bedrock returns `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (`providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:262`), and the spec proposes `Vec<ModelEvent>`. Fine locally, but the conformance follow-up should pick one; say which.
- **Adjacent stale comments** — `chat.rs:120` and `chat.rs:179` say "async-openai 0.40"; `Cargo.lock` pins 0.41.3. Since change 5 already edits comments in this file, sweeping these is free.
- **A cancellation race changes shape** — If the token fires between the finish chunk and EOF, the new code emits no `Finish` where the old code already had. This is contract-correct (`core/src/model.rs:65-67`) and benign in-repo (`ModelTurnAccumulator` defaults `finish_reason` to `Stop`), but it belongs in the Exit-path table as a delta rather than as an unremarked row.

### QUESTIONS

- Was the trailing-usage ordering confirmed against `api.openai.com`, or only against LiteLLM? The ticket generalises to "OpenAI"; the evidence is one proxy's mock backend. If it can't be confirmed, say so in the spec rather than letting the fixture name imply it.
- `ModelSettings` has no `n` field and `build_request` never sets one, so `n > 1` can only arrive from a nonstandard proxy. Should the translator *warn* when it sees a second distinct `finish_reason` (i.e. genuinely ambiguous multi-choice), rather than silently last-wins?
- Should the OpenAI driver tolerate an unparseable chunk the way Gemini does (log + `continue`) instead of terminating the stream? This directly affects the SMA-451 proxy audience the design section invokes as its motivation.
- The Responses immunity argument as written ("they cannot be split across chunks") is true but fragile. The durable invariant is "`Usage` is constructed *only* inside `terminal_events`, which unconditionally appends `Finish`". Should that be recorded as a comment/test so a future arm that emits partial usage doesn't silently break it?
- `ResponseFailed`/`ResponseError` yield `Err` with no `Finish` (`responses.rs:408-426`) — I checked this against the core contract and it is consistent (core mandates that `Finish` is terminal, never that it is mandatory). The spec's "verified immune" note should state this explicitly, since "is there a path with no terminal event at all?" is the exact question the issue asked to discharge.

## What's good

- **Every line reference in the spec is accurate** — I spot-checked eight (`core/src/model.rs:55-63` and `:65-67`, `chat.rs:242-303` and `:237-241`, `responses.rs:441-483`, `gemini/src/model.rs:150,156`, `bedrock/src/stream.rs:14-22`, `chat_streaming.rs:25-33`) and all resolve to what the spec says they do. That is rarer than it should be.
- **The three hardest technical claims are correct, and I verified each independently.** (1) `async-openai` 0.41.3 does consume `[DONE]` internally and ends iteration — `client.rs:811-813` (wasm `unfold` → `None`) and `client.rs:860-862` (non-wasm task `break` → channel close → `None`), so the `None` arm really is the single finish site. (2) The "behaviourally invisible against the current fixtures" argument is exactly right: tracing `consume` over `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt:13` gives `[Usage, Finish]` before and `[Usage]` + `[Finish]` after — an identical emitted sequence. That argument is the strongest thing in the document and it holds. (3) The Responses backend is genuinely immune: `Usage` is only ever built inside `terminal_events` (`responses.rs:455-462`), which unconditionally pushes `Finish` at `:481`, and no other arm emits `Usage`.
- **The release / README / mdBook calls are all correct.** `ChatTranslator` is `pub(crate)` (`chat.rs:216`) inside a private `mod backend` (`src/lib.rs:22`), the crate exports only `OpenAiModel`/`OpenAiModelBuilder`/`BuildError` (`lib.rs:29-30`), the openai README says nothing about usage or ordering, and `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:55-57` documents `Finish` as terminal without asserting any `Usage` position — so no book edit is owed. The no-manual-bump call also matches CLAUDE.md's already-released-crate rule. The `.gitattributes` analysis (CRLF still parses because wiremock hands bytes to a real SSE parser) is likewise correct, and adding the rule as defence-not-fix is the right call, honestly framed.
That's a strong critique, and its BLOCKER contradicts something I told you confidently. I don't take subagent findings at face value — verifying the load-bearing claims myself:

content.text:
All four verified — the challenger is right on every count, including the one that contradicts me:

- **Bedrock has an EOF flush**: `stream.rs:262` `fn finish()`, called at `model.rs:107-112`, doc-commented *"so the consumer always sees a terminal Finish"* — with tests named `finish_flushes_pending_stop_reason_without_metadata`.
- **Anthropic** is the provider that actually lacks one: its only `fn finish*` is `finish_or_error` (a mapping helper), never called from its driver's bare `None => return`.
- **The agent loop drains to `None`**, so nothing in-repo under-counts today.
- **`chat_wire.rs:34-41`** is a *third* instance of the impossible shape — and states the false claim in prose.

**Correction to what I told you earlier: I said Bedrock had a latent truncation gap and used that as a selling point for the design. That was wrong — Bedrock already solved it, more completely than I credited. The gap is in Anthropic.** The chosen approach still stands, but on simplicity rather than on Bedrock being broken.

Folding the justified findings into the spec:

### Multi-choice: a behaviour change, not a preserved invariant

An earlier draft claimed last-wins is "preserved exactly". It is not, and the
difference is worth stating because it is an unclaimed *benefit*.

`finish_event` today is a **per-`consume` local** (`chat.rs:244`, pushed at
`:298`), so the current code emits one `Finish` **per chunk carrying any
`finish_reason`**. Moving the stash to a struct field collapses that to exactly
one `Finish` at EOF. Concretely, for chunks

```text
A: choices:[{index:0, delta:{},            finish_reason:"stop"}]
B: choices:[{index:1, delta:{content:"x"}}]
C: choices:[{index:1, delta:{},            finish_reason:"length"}]
```

old emits `Finish(Stop), TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`; new emits
`TokenDelta, Finish(Length)`. The old sequence puts a `TokenDelta` *after* a
`Finish` — itself a contract violation. The same divergence appears in the far
likelier single-choice case where a proxy repeats `finish_reason` on the usage
chunk (LiteLLM does not, per Appendix A.1 — but that is one proxy).

New semantics, stated plainly: **exactly one `Finish` per stream; the last
`finish_reason` observed anywhere in the stream wins.** Pinned by a unit test.

`ModelSettings` exposes no `n` field and `build_request` never sets one, so
`n > 1` can only arrive from a nonstandard proxy. The translator emits a
`tracing::debug!` when it observes a *second, distinct* `finish_reason`, so
genuinely ambiguous multi-choice is visible in a trace rather than silently
resolved.

### Rejected: pair `[Usage, Finish]` on the usage event (the Bedrock pattern)

**Correction to an earlier draft of this spec.** It asserted that Bedrock emits
no `Finish` when the trailing `Metadata` event never arrives, and used that as
the reason to reject its pattern. **That is false.** Bedrock already has the
same EOF flush proposed here: `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:262`
(`pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self) -> Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>`,
documented as flushing "when the Bedrock stream ends normally (EOF) without
having emitted a `Metadata` event"), driven from
`providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:107-112`, and covered by
`finish_flushes_pending_stop_reason_without_metadata` (`stream.rs:768`).
Bedrock is a **hybrid** — pair-on-`Metadata` *plus* EOF flush — and is not
vulnerable to the failure the earlier table attributed to it.

The real reason to prefer the Gemini shape for OpenAI is **simplicity**: one
emission site and one piece of state, versus Bedrock's `pending_stop_reason` /
`metadata_seen` interaction, which exists because Bedrock must also handle
`Metadata` arriving *before* `MessageStop`. The OpenAI wire has no such
reordering, so that machinery would be dead weight.

Appendix A.2 (no usage chunk at all) still matters — it is why the terminal
event must be anchored to EOF rather than to the usage chunk — but it
discriminates against a *naive* pair-on-usage design, not against Bedrock as
actually implemented.

### The error arm discards a buffered `Finish` — a deliberate behaviour change

The `Some(Err(_))` and cancellation arms do **not** call `finish()`. For
cancellation this is mandated (`core/src/model.rs:65-67`). For the error arm it
is a **change from today's behaviour** and must be recorded as one: currently,
a stream that errors *after* the finish chunk has already delivered `Finish`
inline, so the consumer sees `Finish, Err`; afterwards it sees `Err` alone.

This is not hypothetical for the proxy audience motivating this work.
`CreateChatCompletionStreamResponse` declares `id`, `choices`, `created`,
`model`, and `object` as non-`Option`, so a proxy omitting `object` on its
trailing usage chunk yields a mid-stream deserialization error — exactly the
shape where the buffered `Finish` is now dropped.

**Decision: discard.** Yielding `Finish` and then `Err` would put an item after
the terminal event, which is the very thing this ticket exists to stop; and a
stream that errored did not complete cleanly, so reporting a clean terminal
reason would be a lie. Pinned by a test with a malformed trailing chunk.

### Exit-path semantics

Δ marks a change from current behaviour.

| Exit | Emitted tail | Δ | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal, usage present | `…Usage, Finish` | Δ (was `…Finish, Usage`) | the fix |
| Usage chunk absent | `…Finish` | — | terminal event still emitted |
| Truncated, no `finish_reason` | `…` (no `Finish`) | — | not a clean stop |
| Transport / parse error after finish chunk | `…Err(_)` | Δ (was `…Finish, Err`) | see above |
| Cancelled after finish chunk | `…` (nothing) | Δ (was `…Finish`) | contract mandates no `Finish` |
| Multi-`finish_reason` stream | one `Finish`, last wins | Δ (was one per chunk) | removes post-`Finish` deltas |

Tests are labelled by what they can actually catch. Only the first is a
regression test in the strict sense; conflating the two categories is how the
original blind spot was rationalised.

**Regression — fails on pre-fix code:**

1. Against `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`: assert `Finish` is the final event,
   that a `Usage` precedes it, that there is **exactly one** `Finish`, and that
   the usage carries the real captured counts (`input_tokens: 8`,
   `output_tokens: 6`). The count assertions matter — without them a translator
   emitting a zeroed `Usage` would pass.

   asserting exactly one `Finish` with last-wins, using the A/B/C chunk
   sequence above. Fails pre-fix, which emits two.

regressing, and are not evidence the bug existed:**

3. No-usage stream (`finish_reason` → EOF) still emits exactly one `Finish`.

   existing `tests/cancellation.rs:22` cancels before the first chunk and does
   not cover this race.

   emits `Err` and no `Finish`, pinning the discard decision above.

pre-fix translator, not merely passing after it. Verified by reverting the
translator locally and recording the red output in the PR body. This is the
whole lesson of the ticket: the existing fixtures demonstrate that a test which
cannot fail on broken code is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage.

   original assertions (finish reasons, tool-call assembly, usage values).

`chat.rs:378-541`, where they need no wiremock; only the fixture-driven and

Verified immune by inspection, no code change. `ResponseCompleted` and
`ResponseIncomplete` both route through `terminal_events()`
(`backend/responses.rs:441-483`), which builds `Usage` and `Finish` from a

State the invariant in its durable form rather than the incidental one:
**`Usage` is constructed only inside `terminal_events`, which unconditionally
appends `Finish` before returning** (`responses.rs:455-462`, `:481`). "They
happen to arrive on the same event" is true but fragile; the above is what a
future arm emitting partial usage would have to break. Record it as a comment
on `terminal_events` so the guarantee is stated where it can be violated.

`ResponseFailed` and `ResponseError` yield `Err` with no `Finish` at all
(`responses.rs:408-426`). This is consistent with the contract, which mandates
that `Finish` be *terminal*, never that it be *mandatory* — the same reasoning
as the Chat error arm above. Stated explicitly because "is there a path with no
terminal event?" is precisely what the issue asked to discharge.

Its misread doc comment at `responses.rs:274-278` is fixed here (change 7);
that is the only edit this backend receives.

1. **Bedrock truncation gap** — no `Metadata` after `MessageStop` yields no
   `Finish`. Includes the same misread "Usage must precede Finish" comment at

input.new_string:
Filed as separate Linear issues:

1. **Anthropic truncation gap** (retargeted — an earlier draft wrongly named
   Bedrock). `providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:161-169` buffers `stop_reason`
   from `message_delta` and emits `Finish` only on `message_stop`, and its
   driver at `providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:113` is a bare `None => return`
   with no EOF flush — its only `fn finish*` is `finish_or_error`, a mapping
   helper that is never called from the driver. A stream truncated between
   `message_delta` and `message_stop` therefore emits `Usage` and no `Finish`,
   where Gemini, Bedrock, and post-fix OpenAI all emit one. Anthropic is the
   sole remaining provider with this gap.
2. **Misread contract comments in Bedrock** — `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:14`
   and `:439` repeat the "Usage must precede Finish" misstatement. The code is
   correct; only the prose is wrong.
3. **Cross-provider conformance** — a shared assertion across all five
   providers that a stream is `Finish`-terminated, that `Usage` (when present)
   precedes it, and specifically that **EOF after an observed stop reason emits
   `Finish`** — the last clause being the one that catches item 1. The
   follow-up should also settle the `finish()` return shape, which currently
   differs three ways: `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (Gemini),
   `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` (Bedrock), and `Vec<ModelEvent>`
   (proposed here, matching this crate's infallible `consume`).

Deliberately **not** taken on here, but worth recording as a real question: the
Gemini driver logs and `continue`s on an unparseable chunk
(`providers-gemini/src/model.rs:159-169`) whereas OpenAI terminates the stream.
Given that proxy compatibility is this design's stated motivation, that
asymmetry deserves its own decision rather than an incidental one.

# SMA-522 — OpenAI `Finish`/`Usage` ordering

**Date:** 2026-08-16
**Issue:** [SMA-522](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-522/openai-provider-emits-finish-before-usage-violating-the-core-event)
**Crate:** `paigasus-helikon-providers-openai`
**Status:** approved

## Problem

`paigasus_helikon_core::Model::invoke` states the event-ordering contract
(`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:55-63`):

> - `Usage` MAY appear anywhere; most providers emit one immediately before
>   `Finish` […] Each `Usage` is a complete snapshot (last-wins) […]
> - `Finish` is the terminal event; nothing follows it.

Only `Finish` is positionally constrained. `Usage` is not.

`ChatTranslator::consume` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:242-303`)
orders `Usage` before `Finish` **within a single chunk**, then appends `Finish`
at the end of the chunk that carried `finish_reason`. With
`stream_options.include_usage: true`, OpenAI does not put usage on that chunk —
it arrives on a **separate trailing chunk**. The provider therefore emits
`Finish` and then `Usage`, on every streaming turn.

A consumer that stops reading at `Finish` — which the contract explicitly
licenses — drops the turn's only usage snapshot.

### Impact, stated accurately

The issue claims SMA-402's cross-turn token summing "silently under-counts
every OpenAI turn". **That is not true of any consumer in this repository**,
and the spec should not repeat it. Every in-repo consumer drains the stream to
`None` before reading usage:

- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:941` — `while let Some(evt) =
  model_stream.next().await { … acc.observe(&ev); … }`, then `acc.finish()`
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:98`
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:222-232` (verbatim
  forward)

So the trailing `Usage` *is* observed today and nothing under-counts. This is a
**contract-conformance fix for external consumers**, plus a genuine secondary
repair (duplicate `Finish` emission — see "Multi-choice" below).

The "stops reading at `Finish`" pattern is nonetheless real, not hypothetical,
and there is an in-repo witness: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:237`
does `ModelEvent::Finish { .. } => break`. It happens to ignore `Usage`
(`_ => {}`), so it is unaffected today — but it is the honest evidence that a
contract-abiding consumer written tomorrow would lose the snapshot.

## Evidence

Reproduced first-hand against a keyless LiteLLM proxy (`main-stable`,
Docker 29.6.2). Full traces in Appendix A. The essential shape:

```text
data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}     ← Finish emitted here
data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{…}}                ← Usage arrives after
data: [DONE]
```

Two details the issue does not record, both confirmed by capture:

1. The usage-bearing chunk still carries `choices: [{index:0, delta:{}}]`, and
   omits the `finish_reason` key entirely (it is absent, not `null`).
2. With `include_usage` omitted, **no trailing usage chunk appears at all** —
   the stream ends `finish_reason` chunk → `[DONE]`. This case is why the
   terminal event must be anchored to EOF.

**Provenance limit, stated up front.** This was confirmed against LiteLLM's
mock backend, **not** against `api.openai.com` — no first-party key was
available. The issue and this spec both generalise to "OpenAI"; the direct
evidence is one proxy. Two things keep that from undermining the work: the
trailing-usage split is what the OpenAI Chat Completions streaming spec

My "Bedrock has a latent gap" claim — which I gave you as a selling point — was wrong. | Rejection rationale rewritten: Gemini's shape wins on **simplicity** (one emission site, no `metadata_seen` machinery), not because Bedrock fails. False follow-up ticket deleted. |
| MAJOR | **The ticket's stated impact is false in-repo.** Every consumer drains to `None` (`agent.rs:941`), so nothing under-counts today. | Restated as a contract-conformance fix for *external* consumers, with the real in-repo witness: `compacting_session.rs:237` does `Finish => break`. |
| MAJOR | **Multi-choice isn't "preserved exactly".** Today emits one `Finish` *per chunk*; new emits one per *stream*. Old code could emit `TokenDelta` after `Finish` — itself a violation. | Documented as a behaviour change and an unclaimed bug fix; pinned by a new unit test. |
| MAJOR | **A third bad fixture** — `chat_wire.rs:34-41` welds usage onto the finish chunk *and states the falsehood in prose*. | Added to scope; comment deleted. |
| MAJOR | **Same misread comment 200 lines away** at `responses.rs:274-278`. | Fixed in this PR (Bedrock's two deferred). |
| MAJOR | **The error arm silently drops the buffered `Finish`** — a real behaviour change I hadn't disclosed. | Decision recorded (**discard**, since `Finish, Err` would put an item after the terminal event) and pinned by a malformed-chunk test. |
| MAJOR | **3 of my 4 tests couldn't fail on broken code** — exactly the failure the ticket is about. | Relabelled: 2 true regressions (incl. token-count assertions so a zeroed `Usage` can't pass), 4 new-code guards, plus cancellation-after-finish and malformed-chunk cases. |
| MAJOR | **Follow-up aimed at the wrong crate** — Anthropic has the truncation gap (`model.rs:113` bare `None => return`; its only `fn finish*` is a mapping helper). | Retargeted to Anthropic. |
| MINOR ×6 | Provenance comments must be SSE `:`-lines; capture is LiteLLM's mock (`choices:[{…}]`) not OpenAI's (`choices:[]`); "verbatim" overclaimed; add `tracing::debug!` on empty `finish()`; three-way `finish()` return-shape divergence; stale "async-openai 0.40" comments. | All folded. |

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**
````

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

## Stage 3 complete — plan written

**`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-16-sma-522-openai-finish-usage-ordering.md`** — 7 tasks, 38 steps, committed.

**Files it will touch (8):**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/backend/chat.rs` | `finish_reason` field, `finish()`, driver arm, 2 doc comments, 4 unit tests, stale-version sweep |
| `src/backend/responses.rs` | 2 doc comments (no code) |
| `tests/chat_wire.rs` | reshape SSE body to real envelope |
| `tests/chat_streaming.rs` | 2 fixture consts, 3 tests |
| `tests/cancellation.rs` | 1 test |
| `tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing*.txt` | 2 new fixtures |
| `tests/fixtures/chat_{parallel_tool_calls,content_filter}.txt` | split finish/usage chunks |
| `.gitattributes` | LF pin for the OpenAI fixture dir |

**The ordering insight that shaped it:** `chat_wire.rs:87-94` *already* asserts "Finish must be the last event" — it passes only because its body encodes the impossible shape. So Task 1 Step 1 reshapes that body **before touching any code**, turning an existing green test red. That's genuine TDD and it makes the mutation check nearly free. Mutation checks are required at three points (Tasks 1, 2, 3), each demanding the failure be *observed and recorded*, not assumed.

**Two deviations from the spec, flagged rather than quietly absorbed:**

1. **The cancel-after-finish-chunk test is dropped.** It isn't reachable — wiremock's `set_delay` delays the *whole* response, so you can't deliver the finish chunk then stall before EOF. Any such test would assert whatever the scheduler did that run. Replaced with a deterministic exactly-one-`Finish` test; the real guarantee is structural (the cancel arms `return` without calling `finish()`) and is documented in the test's own comment.
2. **I caught a bug in my first draft of the plan** — that test called `.set_delay()` twice, the second silently overriding the first. Fixed before commit.

Everything else in the spec maps to a task; the coverage table at the bottom of the plan lists all 21 items.

**Recommendation: subagent-driven** (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`), a fresh subagent per task with review between. Inline execution is meant for ~1-2 trivial tasks; this isn't that.

One thing I'll enforce on every dispatch, from prior experience in this repo: implementers must work **synchronously in the foreground** and not end their turn mid-task by backgrounding a long `cargo` run — that failure mode has previously left tests added with no implementation and nothing committed.

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
